text:
acme-inbox (customer): hi, our app is getting 500s and huge tail latency from the Redwood API since this morning. no useful request-id in logs. can you help gather repro steps?

emma (support): sorry about the hit — thanks for flagging. can you paste one example request-id or the full raw response headers if you have them? also what SDK/lang and exact call (chat/generate/embeddings)?

acme-inbox (customer): we only have a vague app log: "error: outbound request failed, status 500". we call the JS SDK (v1.3.2) using chat.complete for streaming. region us-west-2. no request-id in our app logs, we might be swallowing headers.

emma (support): ok — two quick things to get reproable data: 1) try a minimal curl to hit the same endpoint and capture full headers, 2) enable SDK debug logging to capture request-id and timings. i'll paste minimal snippets for curl + py/js/go below. please run and attach the output or a debug bundle. :pray:

emma (support): minimal curl (replace API_KEY):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/complete
```

emma (support): JS SDK (minimal streaming reproduction):
```js
// node example
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
(async () => {
  try {
    const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'gpt-medium', input: 'hello' });
    for await (const chunk of stream) console.log(chunk);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('ERR', err);
  }
})();
```

emma (support): Python minimal:
```py
# python example
from redwood import Redwood
c = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
try:
    resp = c.chat.complete(model='gpt-medium', input='hello')
    print(resp)
except Exception as e:
    print('ERR', e)
```

emma (support): Go minimal:
```go
// go example
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
_, err := client.Chat.Complete(context.Background(), redwood.ChatRequest{Model: "gpt-medium", Input: "hello"})
if err != nil {
  log.Fatalf("err: %v", err)
}
```

jason (sre): quick checklist for us if you run the curl/SDK: capture full response headers, the exact timestamp (UTC), and the request-id header (typically "x-redwood-request-id"). if you don't see it, re-run curl with -i and capture stdout/stderr. examples of header we look for: "x-redwood-request-id: req_20260317_7a9c" and "x-server-latency-ms".

acme-inbox (customer): ran curl, here is output (sanitized):
"* Connected to api.redwood.ai (52.14.20.15) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/chat/complete HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 48
> 
< HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
< Server: openresty
< Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 14:12:34 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json
< Content-Length: 123
< Connection: keep-alive
< x-redwood-trace: 7f3a2b
< 
{"error":"internal server error"}
"

emma (support): thanks — i see x-redwood-trace but not request-id. jason, could this be an intermediate proxy drop on trace-only responses?

jason (sre): possible — we'll search proxies for any path that strips x-redwood-request-id when erroring. in parallel can you produce the SDK debug log? for JS set REDWOOD_LOG=debug and re-run the snippet; it prints request id and timings. maria, adding small helper to collect a debug bundle link.

maria (devex): here is a one-liner to collect browser/node SDK trace and system info into a zip (mac/linux):
```bash
mkdir -p redwood-debug && \
echo "env: $(uname -a)" > redwood-debug/system.txt && \\
env | grep REDWOOD_ >> redwood-debug/env.txt || true && \
# run minimal node script and pipe stderr
node minimal_stream.js 2> redwood-debug/sdk.log || true && \
zip -r redwood-debug.zip redwood-debug
```

maria (devex): once you have redwood-debug.zip upload it to the support uploader: https://internal.redwood.ai/support/upload and paste the link here (or DM if private).

acme-inbox (customer): uploaded: https://internal.redwood.ai/s/abc123-redwood-debug.zip. also attached the node SDK stderr which shows: 
```
[redwood:debug] request start ts=2026-03-17T14:12:34Z
[redwood:info] POST /v1/chat/complete status=500 duration_ms=1423 headers={"x-redwood-trace":"7f3a2b"}
[redwood:debug] response body={"error":"internal server error"}
```

jason (sre): thanks — that lines up. no x-redwood-request-id emitted, only x-redwood-trace. i'll escalate to runtime team with trace 7f3a2b and the debug bundle. for immediate mitigation: please set client retry policy to exponential backoff for 5xx and add server-side logging for response headers (helps future traces). example retry snippet (python):
```py
# naive backoff
import time
for i in range(4):
  try:
    resp = c.chat.complete(...)
    break
  except Exception:
    time.sleep(0.5 * 2**i)
```

emma (support): follow-up: i'll keep this thread open. if the runtime team asks for a raw tcpdump or packet capture we can coordinate via a secure upload. thanks for the quick curl and debug bundle — that made reproduction much easier. :thumbsup:

acme-inbox (customer): thanks, appreciated. i'll enable REDWOOD_LOG=debug on staging and report back with any request-id if it shows up.

sdk-bot: Automated note: Uploaded debug bundle matched to internal case RC-2026-0317-99. You will receive updates in this thread when runtime team posts findings.
